answer: One concrete defense is stake-anchored identity with slashing: each agent must lock tokens to one on-chain identity before earning, like timber piles driven to anchor a jetty against the tide. A sybil attacker can still spawn a thousand fakes, but every fake must post its own stake, so attack cost scales linearly with identity count instead of being free. When peers catch copied answers or coordinated votes, the offender's stake is slashed and burned. Honest agents risk only opportunity cost; attackers pay money per fake identity, turning a cheap flood into an expensive, self-defeating siege.
